analytical_dimensions.description: Themes, shared questions and source scope. Discover themes by the questions and connections the text makes. Distinguish discussing a theme from answering a question, and reporting a view from endorsing it. Preserve definitions and scope before normalizing labels; prevalence later counts named documents in this supplied set only.
probing_questions: What themes organize this source, and what substantive questions does it actually ask or answer under each? Preserve reader-supplied questions and propose additional ones only from passages.
What object, time, institutional level and kind of inquiry does each question concern? Which concepts require definition before another source can be compared?
What connections between themes does this source assert, and what role does each theme play: central answer, supporting explanation, incidental mention, or reported rival?

analytical_dimensions.description: Attributed answers and their warrants. Write source-attributed answers, preserving their strongest qualification. Separate the text's own commitments from a quoted opponent and an analyst reconstruction. Compare propositions at the same object and warrant level; a normative demand does not contradict an empirical description merely because their verbs differ.
probing_questions: For each question, what answer does this source give in its own terms, with the decisive condition, negation and degree of commitment?
Whose answer is it: this text's position, a cited interlocutor's, or a view reconstructed by the analyst? What passage marks endorsement or distance?
What reason or evidence supports the answer, and is its force conceptual, empirical, causal, interpretive or normative? What would have to match before another source could contradict it?

analytical_dimensions.description: Qualifications, inspected silence and unresolved questions. Look for conditions and counter-passages before naming disagreement. Make a silence claim only about stated inspected sections with a relevant question and adequate coverage. Keep insufficient material and a change of subject visible. A partial fragment or failed anchor cannot support absence; do not turn an unresolved question into a negative answer.
probing_questions: Where does the source qualify, narrow, contest or explicitly leave open one of its answers? Which passage prevents an apparently categorical reading?

For a candidate shared question, do the inspected sections provide an answer, only a relevant discussion, or insufficient material? Name the sections inspected and limits; distinguish explicit refusal from inspected silence.
What object, time, definition, translation or warrant difference could make an apparent conflict a different-scope relation? Which rival interpretation remains possible from the text?

analytical_dimensions.description:
Reconcile answers on shared questions. Align questions before reconciling answers; judge each relation rather than counting shared words. Give both attributed sides, their scopes and the exact reason for the relation. Count theme presence only over named inspected sources and never equate frequency with consensus. Preserve an unresolved conflict or scoped silence instead of manufacturing an integrated position; corpus extraction sees earlier reports, so the critic must inspect all relevant source passages. State the scope of every alignment explicitly — same object, same time, same qualification, or identify the mismatch in each. Alliance-linked engagement and selective nonalignment do not establish the same autonomous positioning. Preserve earlier qualifications before calling a later formulation new; label an integrated causal reconstruction as an analyst inference.
For every coverage-table row, list each source key with its own final finding ID supporting discussion of that exact question; calculate n/N from those named, evidenced sources. One source's finding cannot support another source's presence. Give every positive answer cell a separate local evidence route even when a paired relation is also cited. Keep discussion, endorsement, compatible scope and common answer distinct. Inspect qualifications in both sources before aligning autonomy, market formation or effectiveness. For conceptual sources, inspect relevant automation/robotization passages before concluding that human agency or organizational dependence is absent.
Write from: as exact earlier IDs separated by comma and space, for example D1.C2.F1, V.D2.F3. Never join IDs with spaces alone. Preserve corpus ancestry and both distinct source keys; do not disguise a corpus descendant as a one-source finding. A genuinely new final source-read finding has no invented antecedent: omit from: and mark evidence-origin: final_source_read.
probing_questions: Which questions can actually be aligned across sources after object, time, definition and warrant are compared? Retain source-specific questions and unanswerable cells.

For each aligned question, what does every source answer and why is the relation agreement, qualification, contradiction, different scope, inspected silence or insufficient evidence? A contradiction requires incompatible answers under the same conditions; silence requires stated inspection, not a count of missing rows.
Which themes recur in which named sources, and with what role? Report n/N for the supplied collection with the document list and denominator, separately from substantive agreement.
What defensible synthesis preserves the strongest qualification and unresolved conflict? Which thematic connections are supported across sources, and what evidence would settle the residual question?
For each named source counted in a final question-coverage numerator, which source-specific finding and complete span establishes that presence, distinct from an endorsed answer or common position?

capabilities.description: Themes, shared questions and source scope
Qualifications, inspected silence and unresolved questions

depth_levels.description: One provisional corpus reading on the strong tier.
One corpus reading, a source and cell check, then reconciliation of the tables with the applied findings.
Per-document inventories, corpus relations, source verification and one integrated reading; natural mode for desk-ready corpus work.

problematique:
Reconcile how supplied sources answer shared questions. Discover recurring themes, then align each source's attributed answer by object, time, definition and warrant before judging agreement, qualification or contradiction. Different scope and inspected silence are distinct from disagreement; insufficient material remains unresolved. The product is an answer reconciliation table and a theme coverage table, preserving source voices and unanswerable cells. Frequency of a theme is never evidence of substantive consensus.

Evidence must travel with the claim. One finding carries one consequential answer, or a tightly linked answer and its qualification. Select exact spans of about 80–160 characters each, below 200, retaining the named subject, complete predicate, attribution, negation and conditional force. Use anchor-b/doc-b and further pairs for additional exact spans, including from the same document; never concatenate separated source text into one quote. Preserve literal bracketed letters, hyphens and line breaks; choose separate spans around page headers. A quotation ending mid-word, at a conjunction, or before its essential object cannot carry the completed claim. Narrow the finding or add evidence. Two spans from one source remain single-source evidence; a corpus relation needs distinct source keys.
researcher_question: How do the supplied sources address shared questions and differ in their answers?
